summary: This note describes the Buick Park Avenue Essence, a concept car designed and engineered by General Motors' Buick division to showcase advanced technology and styling. It was first shown in 1989 in light green metallic and later toured auto shows in a light white finish. The note also notes its design foreshadowed the production Park Avenue, introduced in 1990.
one_line: The Buick Park Avenue Essence, a 1989 GM concept car that previewed the production Park Avenue of 1990.
key_facts: The Buick Park Avenue Essence was a concept car designed and engineered by the Buick division of General Motors.
The Buick Park Avenue Essence was designed to showcase advanced technology and styling.
The Essence was first shown in 1989 in a light green metallic color.
The Essence later made rounds through the auto show circuits in a light white color.
The Essence's interior included a wide, sweeping instrument panel.
The instrument panel of the Essence housed a prototype Delco Navicar navigation system among other innovations.
The Essence's smooth, graceful body lines forecast the eventual production Park Avenue.
The production Park Avenue was introduced in 1990.
The Essence was powered by the then-new 165 hp version of Buick's 3800 OHV V6 engine.
